A borrower takes a $20,000 loan at 6% annual interest compounded monthly (a 0.5% monthly rate) on a 60-month level-payment schedule. On top of the scheduled payment, the borrower pays an extra $100 of principal every month starting in month 1. Each month interest accrues on the outstanding balance first, then the scheduled payment and the extra $100 are applied to principal. Work to exact cents; the final payment is whatever amount clears the remaining balance.

What is the scheduled monthly payment (ignoring the extra principal)? Give your answer in dollars to the nearest cent.
items.output:
To find the scheduled monthly payment (ignoring the extra principal), we first need to calculate the monthly interest rate (0.5%) and the total number of payments (60 months).

Monthly interest rate (i) = 6% / 12 = 0.005 (as a decimal)
Monthly interest rate (i) = 0.005 (as a decimal)
Monthly interest rate (i) = 0.5 (as a percentage)

Total number of payments (n) = 60 months

Loan amount (P) = $20,000

Monthly payment (M) can be calculated using the formula for monthly payments on a loan:

M = P × i × (1 + i)^n × ((1 + i)^n - 1) / ((1 + i)^n × (1 + i) - (1 + i))

M = 20000 × 0.005 × (1 + 0.005)^60 × ((1 + 0.005)^60 - 1) / ((1 + 0.005)^60 × (1 + 0.005) - (1 + 0.005))

M ≈ 379.02 (rounded to the nearest cent)

So, the scheduled monthly payment (ignoring the extra principal) is approximately $379.02.
